title: Arman Financial Services Ltd - 531179 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Microfinance lender exiting credit stress: Q4 disbursements INR738 crores (+88% YoY) and PAT INR41 crores, but opex/asset near 9% and FY27 credit cost guided around 3%.

summary.headline: Arman Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 220% YoY to INR41 crore on lower credit costs, with AUM at a record INR2,728 crore (+22% YoY).
summary.overview: Management said the microfinance industry has moved past its most difficult phase, with collection efficiency and borrower behaviour improving from the second half of FY26. Consolidated AUM reached a record INR2,728 crore (+22% YoY) and quarterly disbursements a record INR951 crore, while FY26 PAT grew 9% to INR57 crore. Management flagged higher opex (microfinance cost-to-assets near 9%) and elevated rejection rates as the price of a stricter individual-level underwriting model. FY27 is framed as disciplined growth with quality over volume, and the call gave no firm profit-peak commitment.

financial_highlights.change: NNPA up from about 0.7% QoQ per analyst

segments.name: Microfinance (Namra, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,999 crore (+19% YoY); Q4 disbursements INR738 crore; FY26 disbursements INR1,798 crore; Q4 gross total income INR117 crore, FY26 INR433 crore; pre-provision operating profit INR41 crore in Q4 and INR143 crore in FY26. Subsidiary CRAR 27.86%.

segments.name: Standalone (MSME, 2W, LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM INR730 crore (+30% YoY), MSME 76% of book. Quarterly disbursements INR213 crore, FY26 INR636 crore. GNPA MSME 3.84%, 2W 3.95%, LAP 0.74%. Standalone CRAR 41%. LAP reached breakeven in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Opex: microfinance cost-to-assets about 9% now, target about 7% in FY27 and about 6% in the short to medium term; absolute FY27 opex expected to rise slightly (up to about 7%).
Credit cost: management called about 3% a reasonable normalised FY27 level; long-term LAP credit cost seen around 2%.
Growth: MSME targeted at about 25% growth in FY27; LAP 20-25%; management said FY27 is not the year to push growth hard.
Returns: ROA aspiration of 3.5-4%+ if growth stays consistent; ROE to rise as leverage increases from low levels, specific targets not disclosed.
Peak profitability in FY27 described as unlikely but 'close'; INR5,000 crore AUM aspiration retained but timing deferred until macro uncertainty eases.
capex_capacity: New MSME branches in Uttar Pradesh opened, with more planned in the current quarter; LAP expansion into UP to follow once stable.
Solar loan pilot launched in Gujarat (rural rooftop solar); management said it is too early to size.
About 90% of microfinance portfolio covered under CGFMU scheme; CGFMU premium now a recurring opex item, capitalised.
Digital collections at about 35% overall and 70%+ for the individual loan portfolio.
demand_pricing: April and May disbursements lower than Q4, as is seasonal; zero-DPD and early delinquencies stable through a hot summer and fuel/LPG disruptions.
Average borrowing cost about 12%; marginal cost about 11.75% over the last two quarters; management expects Q3 cost of borrowing at similar or lower levels.
No change in microfinance lending rates since last quarter; yield movement attributed to product mix (LAP cheaper than MSME; individual vs JLG pricing).
Rejection rates remain elevated as underwriting moved from JLG to individual evaluation; credit and recovery separated from branches.
LAP competition rising from NBFCs, MFIs and SFBs; South India (Telangana) penetration slow in saturated market.
Management sees lower MFI competition as some larger players face liquidity or capital issues, while several are raising volumes again.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of borrowing trajectory and NIM risk for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost about 12%, marginal about 11.75%; management expects cost at similar or lower levels in Q3, though not fully insulated from MCLR rises.

qa_highlights.question: Opex to asset target?
qa_highlights.answer: Microfinance cost-to-assets about 9% versus a low of about 5%; target about 7% this year, with a 6% medium-term goal. Absolute opex to rise slightly, up to about 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost for FY27 normalised year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3% is a ballpark good number and should be achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Is GNPA going up under CGFMU?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, gross NPA may rise because assets cannot be written off until the guarantee claim is settled; net NPA and provision coverage (about 92%) stay intact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NNPA rise from about 0.7% to 0.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Early-stage write-offs in the last two years lowered staging, so lower provisions are needed; CGFMU cover also lowers provisioning. Management said all segments remain below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sales team push back on the tighter credit model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the field team welcomed the collection relief and expects pushback from sales as conditions improve; it sees this as a culture and communication task.

risks_watch: Gross NPA likely to rise under CGFMU claim process even as net NPA stays controlled.
Elevated rejection rates and a large individual-level credit team may keep opex above target.
LAP GNPA at 0.74% with early 90+ cases appearing in a new book growing 20-25%.
Macro pressures (West Asia conflict, fuel and LPG disruption, inflation) could delay the collection recovery.
Borrowing costs could rise if MCLR increases; part of the book is fixed rate.
Elevation Capital still holds about 8% stake, with exit timing undisclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and collections recovery, but cautious on growth and profit outlook: management repeatedly declined to give firm FY27 targets and tied the INR5,000 crore AUM aspiration to macro stabilisation.
key_quotes: Consolidated profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR41 crores, registering a growth of 85% sequentially and 220% year-on-year.
It may be possible to bring it down to, let's say, around 6% in the short to medium term.
And MSME as well, we are targeting somewhere around 25 %-odd growth in FY27.
So this is probably not the year to push growth or push growth hard at least.

growth.why: Management guides MSME growth of about 25% and LAP growth of 20-25% in FY27, with opex/assets falling from about 9% to about 7%, but says FY27 is not the year to push growth hard and gives only partial backing via new UP branches and a Gujarat solar pilot with no sizing.
